q: In physics, work specifies the action (____) and the movement produced by the force.
e: Work in physics is specifically defined by the application of a force that results in movement.

q: Work is said to be done when a ____ produces motion.
e: Motion must be produced by a force for work to be considered done in a physics context.

q: Work is defined as the product of force and ____ moved in the direction of the force.
e: The definition of work requires both a force and a displacement in the direction of that force.

q: The mathematical expression for work done when force and distance are in the same direction is ____.
e: This is the fundamental formula for work when the force and displacement vectors are parallel.
Work has magnitude but no specific direction, classifying it as a scalar quantity.

q: The SI unit of work is the ____.
e: The standard International System (SI) unit for measuring work is the joule (J).

q: 1 joule of work is done when a force of 1 ____ moves an object through a distance of 1 metre in the direction of the force.
e: A joule is defined as the work done by a force of one newton acting over a distance of one metre.

q: When the unit of force is in pound (lb) and the distance is in foot (ft), the unit of work is ____.
e: In the imperial system, work is measured in foot-pounds (ft-lb).

q: When the unit of force is in dyne and the distance is in centimetre, the unit of work is ____.
e: In the CGS system, the unit of work is the erg.

q: The relationship between the joule and the erg is ____.
e: One joule is equivalent to ten million ergs.

q: When the force is constant and makes an angle with the direction of motion, work is defined as ____.
e: This formula accounts for the component of the force that acts in the direction of the displacement.

q: When the directions of the force and the motion are the same, the angle is ____ and work done is $W=Fs$.
e: When force and motion are parallel, the angle is zero, making the cosine term equal to 1.

q: When the force and the motion are in opposite directions, the angle is ____ and work done is $W=-Fs$.
e: When force opposes motion, the angle is 180 degrees, making the cosine term equal to -1.

q: When the force and the motion are perpendicular to each other, the angle is ____ and work done is zero.
e: When force is perpendicular to motion, the cosine of 90 degrees is zero, resulting in no work done.
